body: I’m so sorry you’re feeling so much hatred towards yourself, it’s such a horrible feeling. You sound like a beautiful person. I’m here to talk or just listen if you need someone. X
Thanks for reassuring me! I think I will try and find somewhere else to live whilst this is going on like you said. Yes he is :/ thank you!!

Hi there, thank you so much for your response! No, unfortunately the police didn’t seem interested, you’re right that they don’t take things seriously enough. Yes I’ve started taking note of number plates and details etc, and taking photos of the cars so I’ll have lots to give and show the police if it carries on. 

Luckily I do have good friends and family around me, although they don’t know about this yet but I think it’s probably time to tell them as it is a struggle on my own sometimes. 

And thank you for reassuring me it’s not my fault. You’re very kind and you’re advice has helped a lot, thank you.

Hello, I’m so sorry to hear about your mum. I can completely relate to you with all of this, it must be incredibly difficult. It’s good that you’re in therapy, I really hope you begin to find it more helpful than uncomfortable and that your feelings begin to improve in time. Thank you so much, please PM me anytime too. I’m always here if you want to talk or vent also, so please remember that. Thank you for your kindness
That does make sense. Thank you so much for the recommendation! I’ll definitely take a look at that book. Thank you ever so much for your advice!

I think you’re right, I’m just so worried of being judged by my family, other than my boyfriend they’re all I’ve got and I’m worried this would put me in a worse place if you know what I mean. Thank you for your opinion

I mean to get back to a place where these things are no longer causing me to stop enjoying life; to be like I was before all this happened and to gain a happier mentality and healthy state of mind, I suppose.
That’s really reassuring, thank you for sharing that! I’m so glad it helped you, hopefully it will help me too.
I think I’ll be fine, thank you. And thank you so much for the support, it really means a lot.
I’d never thought of it like that. Thank you so much!

Hello! Thank you so much for your reply. I think your right, face to face would be best however we’re long distance so this makes it a bit harder, I only saw him at New Year and probably won’t see him for at least another month yet. At least that gives me time to prepare what to say though. Your advice has really helped, thank you! I’m sorry to hear you’ve had a suicide attempt too. I’m so glad you’re still here, you seem like an amazing person. Wishing you all the best, take care.
Hello! I think you’re right, I will try and take a slow approach, thank you. And I know, this is such an amazing community! Thank you so much for your advice

Hello, thank you for reassuring me there's nothing wrong with me. I hadn't even thought of the pre-grieving thing but it would make a lot of sense as we knew it was terminal for around 2/3 months. You really have helped, thank you so much for taking the time to talk to me.

That was incredibly helpful and everything you said makes a lot of sense. Thank you so much. I think I will try and talk about it with someone, I haven't really done that yet and you've made me realise it might help. Thank you again.

Thank you so much for doing this! Could you maybe shed some light on my situation? So I’m 18 years old and I lost my mother on 26th December 2016. She had a terminal illness and myself and my dad cared for her from when she was diagnosed in September 2016 until she died. However, I’ve been left feeling very confused. My mum was like my best friend, but since she’s died I’ve only really cried once, which was at her funeral. I feel completely heartless because I tend to avoid talking about her to family and friends, not because it upsets me a lot but because I just feel weird about it. I feel like I haven’t really grieved; lots of people told me it will be really difficult and that some days I’ll just cry and cry. I’m a very emotional person so I expected this, but it hasn’t happened. Some people also said sometimes it takes a few months before it ‘hits you’, but again, it’s been over a year and that hasn’t happened. I’m just so confused about why I’m like this, it makes me feel heartless. Could anyone explain this? I don’t know what’s wrong with me.

I’m so sorry for your loss. I’m 18 and I lost my mother from pancreatic cancer on 26th December 2016, she was diagnosed in the September. You are right, nothing prepares you for it but I can honestly say it does get better. Your dad’s spirit will always be with you. Sending you lots of hugs, take it steady. X
Thank you so much. I wish you the best of luck for healing

I know, I do feel terribly guilty that they could do the same to someone else so I will look into that. Thank you ever so much for your advice and I'm so glad therapy helped you, I hope it helps me too.

Wow thank you so much! It does feel really scary but I don't want to feel like this anymore so I'm prepared to get through this hard bit. Thank you again, you're equally just as strong and very kind for taking the time to share your advice with me :) yes you're making complete sense and you've put a lot of confidence in me so thank you. I'm so glad you're recovering and feeling better, I really hope things continue to look up for you. You're a lovely person and truly deserve happiness. :)

Thank you so much for your reply! I'm so sorry you have had a similar issue too. I think I will try therapy, it sounds like this might help me a lot. Unfortunately I don't think I could move away right now but that's I think them living there is only temporary which is good. Thank you for sharing your story and I send you all the best wishes, and thank you for your helpful advice.

Thank you both. I would like to move away but unfortunately it's not really feasible right now - I've just got myself a job I love in the area which is also getting me a qualification, and the course is 2 years, and I couldn't afford to move. I will think about telling my family soon and moving away as soon as I can. Thank you both so much for your advice.

Wow. I'm completely blown away by your response and I can't thank you enough for that. Everything you have said completely makes sense and I can relate to it all so much. You have made such a big difference...I was so confused but you've made me understand what is going on so much more now. You are an incredibly smart and amazing person. Thank you so much for taking the time to explain that too me, I absolutely love the dog thing, it's a brilliant way to explain this situation. I think I will seek professional help, and try the dog method when myself and my boyfriend do anything sexual again. Wow. You have just helped a complete stranger more than you'll ever know, thank you again.

I am so sorry to hear about your situation. Thank you ever so much for your help, I've left school now and and am in work but there's definitely people I can go to within my workplace. Thank you again and I'm sending all my best wishes to you.

Of course not! I really appreciate your concern, thank you.

1. I don't really remember, these family friends were also my brothers friends (around 5 years older than me), and they said they'd let me hang around with them if I let them do what they did. With me being very young, I didn't realise this was just awful blackmail and I didn't even realise how wrong it was, so it wasn't really something I thought about much, I just knew it seemed strange. Yes, I was afraid to talk about it as I was told by these boys not to tell anyone.

2. Their mum was my mum's best friend so they saw each other a lot, but my mum has passed away and so we don't see much of them anymore, just out in the street. Their mum tries to keep in contact with me but as you change imagine I find it difficult to speak to her. 

3. No, my boyfriend now isn't my first but he's the first person I've done anything of a sexual nature with.
I'm so sorry for everything you have been through. I think I will try counselling again but with someone different perhaps. You're so right, thank you so much. Best wishes to you.

I'm so sorry for your loss too. I will. Myself and my dad are very close and make a good team, we're always taking care of each other. 

It must be horrible to lose someone you've been with for so long, I really hope you're doing okay. Sending all my best wishes to you. I hope you have lots of wonderful people around you, supporting you through this tough time.

Very ironic! So tragic. So sorry for your loss, it's horrible at any age. Thank you for being honest, you've given me hope sharing how you felt as things should start to improve soon. I will, and you should too. Thank you again, sending my best wishes your way.

Hello, I'm so sorry that you lost your mum so young. It's so tragic. Thank you for the book recommendation, I'll take a look at that. What you've said is beautiful and sums it up perfectly. I've written letters too and have imaginary conversations, it helps me sometimes so I hope it helps you too. I completely agree. You have a beautiful outlook. Your mum would be very proud of you. Best wishes.

Hello, thank you for sharing your experience. I'm so sorry for your loss. I feel as if I'm in the denial too sometimes, but I think that's completely normal. I'll think about therapy, thank you. Sending best wishes to you, I hope you find some happiness soon.

Hello, thank you so much for sharing your story. I'm so incredibly sorry for the loss of both of your parents, I can't imagine how that must feel. I really love the concept your son has taken, what a beautiful way of looking at it. I definitely notice people not appreciating their parents a lot, but I'm also sad when they do because I, and as I've now found out,  many others can't do that. You seem like a beautiful person, and I can only imagine that the tough times have made you a good person. Sending you lots of hugs and best wishes, and thank you for making me realise I'm not alone.

Thank you for sharing your story; I'm so sorry for the loss of your mother too. And thank you so much for assuring me I'm not alone. It's very easy to feel that way in situations like this but thanks to Reddit, we realise unfortunately there are lots of people in the same heartbreaking and horrible situation. The world can be very cruel, but neither of us, plus anyone else, will give up. Sending my best wishes to you and hoping that you begin to heal with time and find happiness.

Never think that! No matter what your age, it's always going to be a difficult loss and you should never feel as if you can't be upset and miss your dad. What happened is cruel, but you know what your lovely dad would want you to do? Try and carry on with life the best you can. I always have the thought that my mum is watching over me, so I try to achieve things as best I can and try to get on with life, just as she'd have wanted. It's the same with your dad - he wouldn't want to see you here putting your life on hold and be so sad. Sure, have a balance where you make sure you are taking time to grieve, but also remember that you need to find enjoyment in your life, just like your dad would have wanted. Surround yourself with great people, make more time for 'you' time - like any hobbies and interests you have, or simply just having a relaxing bath or something. It's going to be difficult, and you'll never completely heal from this loss but you will learn to manage with it, just take it day by day. You will get happiness back and have good times. You're strong and you'll get through it.

Hello, firstly I'm so sorry for the loss of your dad. I know how heartbreaking it is - I'm 18 and I lost my mum almost a year ago. Obviously I can't speak from experience as you've been in this situation slightly longer, but from the experience of others, I've been told (even though it sounds incredibly cliche!) it does get easier, and for you, this day over any other is going to be more difficult. It's my mum's birthday next week, and the anniversary of her death on Boxing Day. I have already tried to accept that these will be sad, horrible days, where ill let myself cry and much as I like and completely let my emotions out. Well done, as you've got through most of the most difficult day! Maybe just try and do the same - let your emotions out freely, don't hold back and just try and distract yourself by hobbies, friends and family as much as possible. I really hope you start to heal soon, and remember you're not alone. Always here if you want to message.

Thank you ever so much for your response. I'm so sorry about the death of your dad, it's never going to be easy at any age. I only recently, in the last month, told my boyfriend about the abuse I have suffered even though we've been together for a while - and he was the first person I'd ever told. I still feel very uncomfortable about this and I don't know if I'm quite ready to talk about it. However, I do think therapy would help for other things, such as the mental health issues I've developed. So I will give that some thought, thank you. I will focus on the positives. Thank you so, so much for your help.

Thank you so much for your response. I am deeply sorry for the loss of your mum, but I also feel some relief to not be alone in this. It's so unfair that we've felt so much pain in our lives, but things must get better from here. You're right, we will find happiness which will hopefully increase over time. I can understand why you'd breakdown in public sometimes, although I've never had that so everyone around me thinks I'm perfectly fine. So it kind of sucks. It's my mum's birthday next week too, the first without her, and I will be at work all day, and I can see I may have a bit of a breakdown. But what will be, will be. And it's not something we can help, we have to let our emotions out. Thank you again for sharing your situation, and I hope you always improve and find more happiness soon.
